_meta.purpose: Per-(micro, LC-id) application notes — explain HOW the micro's strategy applies to that specific problem. Surfaced in the UI as the anchor chip's tooltip. Audit batch grows over time; see git log.
_meta.status: Audit passes 1-4 — covers 20 micros (~145 notes). Latest pass added: bs-textbook, bs-on-answer, dfs-tree-orders, post-order-depth, topo-sort.

complement-lookup.1: Two-Sum unsorted. One pass, deferred insert: check map for (target-x) FIRST, then store x→i. Guarantees we don't pair x with itself.
complement-lookup.167: Two-Sum on SORTED array. Hash works but is suboptimal — converging two-pointer (tp-k-sum) is O(1) space. Listed here for the universal pattern.
complement-lookup.653: Two-Sum in a BST. Two clean approaches: (a) collect inorder→array then complement-lookup; (b) two iterators (inorder + reverse-inorder) converging — O(h) space.
complement-lookup.560: Subarray sum = K with negatives. Prefix-sum + complement: map[prefix] = count; for each prefix, answer += map[prefix-K]; then ++map[prefix]. Same complement-lookup engine over prefix space.
complement-lookup.974: Subarray sum divisible by K. Same prefix+complement, but key on (prefix mod K) (normalise negative mods). The complement is just the SAME residue (we want differences ≡ 0 mod K).

freq-counter.387: First unique char. Counter pass over s; second pass returns first idx where count[s[i]]==1.
freq-counter.169: Majority element. Counter works O(n) space; Boyer-Moore voting is the optimal O(1) — same conceptual frequency-tracking, just collapsed to two vars.
freq-counter.49: Group anagrams. Counter form: 26-int tuple as group key. Beats sort-key when k (word length) is large.
freq-counter.242: Valid anagram. Compare two 26-counters; or single counter with += and -=, check all zero.
freq-counter.567: Permutation in string. Sliding window of len(s1) over s2; track 'matched chars' so the window-check is O(1) per slide.
freq-counter.229: Majority Element II (> n/3). Boyer-Moore generalised to 2 candidates + final verification pass.
freq-counter.350: Intersection 2 arrays II (with multiplicity). Counter on smaller array; iterate larger, decrement and emit on hit.
freq-counter.819: Most common word (excluding banned). Tokenise, lowercase, strip punct; counter over words ∖ banned; argmax.
freq-counter.1153: String transforms into another. Mapping s[i]→t[i] must be a function (single-valued). If s==t trivial; else need an unused 27th char (≤25 distinct in t) for the temporary cycle break.
freq-counter.1657: Determine if two strings are close. Op1+Op2 preserve: (a) SET of chars must match exactly, (b) SORTED freq multiset must match.
freq-counter.266: Palindrome permutation. Counter; ≤ 1 char with odd count.
freq-counter.1481: Least unique ints after K removals. Counter, sort COUNTS ascending, greedily consume smallest-count keys with budget K.
freq-counter.734: Sentence similarity. Word-pair set (both directions); walk word-by-word, check membership.

seen-set.217: Contains duplicate. One pass; add to set; on first re-encounter return true.
seen-set.219: Contains duplicate within K indices. Sliding-window set of size K+1: add cur, evict at i-K, check membership before add.
seen-set.287: Find duplicate. Seen-set is O(n) space — works but Floyd's tortoise/hare (tp-fast-slow tag) gives O(1) space — that's the optimal.
seen-set.141: Linked List cycle. Seen-set O(n) space — Floyd's two-pointer (tp-fast-slow tag) is O(1) optimal. Both tagged so the comparison is visible.
seen-set.1488: Avoid flood. Map lake→last-rain-day; sorted set of dry days; on rain to a wet lake, bisect for the next dry day to drain. (Hash + binary-search combo — could warrant a sub-micro.)
seen-set.1452: People whose list contains all of another. For each list build set; outer loop, subset-check via .issubset / all-in.

dp-1d-linear.70: Climbing stairs. dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Two rolling vars; O(1) space.
dp-1d-linear.198: House robber. dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + a[i]). Two rolling vars.
dp-1d-linear.213: House robber II (circular). Two passes: rob houses [0..n-2] OR [1..n-1] (exclude first or last); max of the two.
dp-1d-linear.91: Decode ways. dp[i] = dp[i-1] (if s[i-1] != '0') + dp[i-2] (if s[i-2..i-1] in 10..26).
dp-1d-linear.139: Word break. dp[i] = ∃ j<i: dp[j] AND s[j..i] ∈ dict. Substring check trie or set.
dp-1d-linear.322: Coin change min. dp[w] = 1 + min(dp[w-c] for c in coins). O(W·n) — unbounded knapsack shape but lives here as the simplest DP intro.
dp-1d-linear.746: Min cost climbing stairs. dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]).
dp-1d-linear.837: New 21 Game. dp[i] = (dp[i-1] + … + dp[i-W])/W; maintain rolling sum to drop the inner loop. Probability variant of climbing-stairs.
dp-1d-linear.403: Frog jump. dp[stone] = set of arrival speeds; transitions {v-1,v,v+1} to stones[stone]+v. Hash-of-sets shape, but still linear DP over stones.
dp-1d-linear.343: Integer break. dp[n] = max over i in 1..n-1 of max(i*(n-i), i*dp[n-i]). O(n²) but technically 1D (knapsack-style).

dfs-template.200: Number of Islands. For each unvisited '1', DFS (mark to '0' or visited set), ++count. Same as dfs-grid-flood — listed under both pre-prune.
dfs-template.695: Max area of island. DFS RETURNS subtree-area (1 + sum of 4 neighbour calls); track global max.
dfs-template.547: Number of provinces. For each unvisited city, DFS via adjacency matrix marking; ++count.
dfs-template.133: Clone graph. Map<orig, clone>; on visit, create clone, recurse to each neighbour, attach. Pure visited-via-map idiom.
dfs-template.417: Pacific Atlantic. Two DFSes from boundary cells (reverse: water flows DOWN-to-UP); mark cells reachable to each ocean; intersect the two boolean grids.
dfs-template.841: Keys and Rooms. DFS from room 0; visited[i]=true; recurse into each key in rooms[i]. Check all visited.
dfs-template.489: Robot Room Cleaner. DFS with MOTION backtracking — for each of 4 directions: clean, move, recurse, move-back, turn. Distinct shape worth own sub-micro if it grows.
dfs-template.1192: Critical Connections (Tarjan). disc[]/low[] arrays; back-edges update low. Bridge when low[v] > disc[u]. (Tarjan deserves its own micro; tracked for future.)
dfs-template.582: Kill Process. Build child-list adjacency; DFS from killPid collecting all descendants.
dfs-template.1376: Time to inform all employees. Build manager→reports adjacency; DFS from head returning max-path-time over subtrees; combine with informTime[u].
dfs-template.1530: Number of good leaf pairs. DFS returns LIST of leaf-distances from current root; for each ancestor, count pairs across left+right with sum ≤ distance.

tp-converging.344: Reverse String. l=0, r=n-1; swap and shrink. O(n/2) ops, O(1) space.
tp-converging.345: Reverse Vowels. Same shape, but skip non-vowels on each side before swapping; only swap when both pointers land on vowels.
tp-converging.977: Squares of Sorted Array. Sorted with possible negatives. Compare |arr[l]| vs |arr[r]|; place larger² at result[end], advance the matching side, decrement end.
tp-converging.925: Long Pressed Name. Two pointers (i on name, j on typed). If chars match advance both; else allow advance j only if typed[j]==typed[j-1] (i.e. long-press repeat). At end, i must equal name.length.
tp-converging.161: One Edit Distance. Walk both strings in parallel; on first mismatch, try one of (replace, insert into shorter, delete from longer) and check rest matches.
tp-converging.243: Shortest Word Distance. Single pass; track lastIdx of word1 and word2; on each hit update min |i - other.lastIdx|.
tp-converging.360: Sort Transformed Array. f(x)=ax²+bx+c is convex (a>0) or concave (a<0). Use 2-ptr from ends; pick the extreme f(l) vs f(r), append, advance.
tp-converging.415: Add Strings. Walk both strings from RIGHT; track carry; prepend each digit-sum % 10; flush carry.
tp-converging.67: Add Binary. Same right-to-left two-pointer + carry, base-2 instead of 10.

dp-2-strings.72: Edit Distance. dp[i][j] = if s1[i-1]==s2[j-1] then dp[i-1][j-1] else 1 + min(insert dp[i][j-1], delete dp[i-1][j], replace dp[i-1][j-1]).
dp-2-strings.583: Delete Operation for 2 Strings. answer = m + n - 2 * LCS(s1, s2). Reduces to 1143.
dp-2-strings.1143: LCS. dp[i][j] = if match dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). Workhorse 2D DP.
dp-2-strings.10: Regex Matching. dp[i][j] for s[0..i] vs p[0..j]. '*' = zero-or-more of prev char: dp[i][j-2] (zero) OR (dp[i-1][j] if prev matches s[i-1]).
dp-2-strings.44: Wildcard Matching. '*' matches zero-or-more ANY chars: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] OR dp[i][j-1]. '?' matches one. Simpler than #10 because '*' isn't tied to prev char.
dp-2-strings.97: Interleaving String. dp[i][j] = can s3[0..i+j] be formed by interleaving s1[0..i] and s2[0..j]? Transition uses s3[i+j-1] matching s1[i-1] OR s2[j-1].
dp-2-strings.115: Distinct Subsequences. dp[i][j] = #ways s[0..i] can form t[0..j]. If match: dp[i-1][j-1] + dp[i-1][j] (use or skip s[i-1]); else dp[i-1][j].
dp-2-strings.727: Min Window Subsequence. dp[i][j] = the START INDEX in S of the smallest window ENDING at S[i] that contains T[0..j]. On match propagate dp[i-1][j-1]; else carry dp[i-1][j].

bfs-shortest-unweighted.127: Word Ladder. BFS over implicit graph (transform 1 char at a time); enqueue 1-step neighbours; return depth when target popped. Bidirectional BFS halves the search (separate sub-micro bfs-bidirectional).
bfs-shortest-unweighted.752: Open the Lock. BFS over 4-digit states; 8 neighbours each (±1 each wheel); skip deadends set; first reach target.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.1091: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix. 8-direction BFS from (0,0) over '0' cells; dist = cells visited. First time you pop (n-1, n-1) is the answer.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.433: Min Genetic Mutation. Word-ladder shape but mutation alphabet is {A,C,G,T}. Bank as the visited set.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.1730: Shortest Path to Get Food. BFS from '*' over '.' cells; the first '#' (food) popped is the answer.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.815: Bus Routes. BFS over (stop, routes-taken). For each stop, enqueue ALL stops of every route serving it; visited set keys on ROUTES not stops to avoid re-traversing same route.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.1197: Min Knight Moves. 8 L-shaped neighbours; (x,y) symmetry means you only need to explore the first octant (use |x|, |y|).
bfs-shortest-unweighted.1284: Min Flips Convert Binary Matrix. Encode matrix as INTEGER (bit per cell); 12 (3x3 max) cells = 2^9 states. Each move XORs a 5-bit mask. BFS over int states; visited set of ints.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.1293: Shortest Path Obstacles Elim. BFS over (row, col, k-erasures-used). State-space BFS — k is the EXTRA dimension. First time (m-1, n-1, *) popped is answer.

monotonic-stack.496: Next Greater Element I. Monotonic decreasing stack on nums2; for each cur, pop while stack-top < cur and store nextGreater[popped] = cur; then look up nums1 in the resulting map.
monotonic-stack.503: Next Greater II (circular). Walk indices i in 0..2n-1, use i % n; same monotonic decreasing stack; only assign answer on FIRST pass through each index.
monotonic-stack.739: Daily Temperatures. Monotonic decreasing stack of INDICES; on each new temp, pop while stack-top temp < cur and set answer[popped] = i - popped.
monotonic-stack.901: Online Stock Span. Monotonic decreasing stack of (price, span). On new price, pop and sum spans while top.price ≤ cur; push (cur, sumSpans + 1).
monotonic-stack.1019: Next Greater Node in Linked List. Materialise to array (one pass) then standard daily-temperatures monotonic stack. Linked-list specific because a single forward walk can't see future.

subset-combination.78: Subsets (no dupes). Backtrack(i): emit path; for j in [i..n): pick a[j], recurse(j+1), un-pick. Iterative bitmask variant: for mask in 0..2^n.
subset-combination.90: Subsets II (with dupes). Sort first. At each depth, skip a[j] if a[j]==a[j-1] AND j>i (avoid emitting the SAME subset twice at the same depth).
subset-combination.39: Combination Sum (each candidate reusable). Same template, but recurse(j) NOT recurse(j+1) — allows re-picking the same element. Prune when sum > target.
subset-combination.40: Combination Sum II (each used once + dupes). Sort + recurse(j+1) + skip-dup-at-same-depth (same trick as #90).
subset-combination.216: Combination Sum III (use digits 1..9, exactly k numbers, sum n). Backtrack with start index 1..9, depth ≤ k, prune if sum > n or remaining can't reach.
subset-combination.491: Increasing Subsequences. Backtrack; only pick if >= last picked; depth-local 'seen values' set to dedupe (can't sort first because we'd lose original order).
subset-combination.77: Combinations (k from n). Backtrack(start, path): if len==k emit; for j in [start..n]: include j, recurse(j+1), exclude.

kadane.53: Max Subarray. cur = max(x, cur + x); best = max(best, cur). Single pass O(n).
kadane.152: Max Product Subarray. Track BOTH cur_max and cur_min (negative × negative flips sign). cur_max' = max(x, x·cur_max, x·cur_min); cur_min similarly.
kadane.918: Max Sum Circular Subarray. Two answers: (a) standard kadane non-wrap; (b) wrap = total − minSubarray. Answer = max(a, b). Edge: all-negative → answer = a (b would be 0).
kadane.1567: Max Length Positive-Product Subarray. Track lengths of (current positive run, current negative run). Walk; reset on zero; swap pos/neg on negative element.

floyd-cycle.141: Linked List Cycle. slow=head, fast=head; both step (slow 1, fast 2). If they ever meet, cycle exists. O(1) extra space.
floyd-cycle.142: Linked List Cycle II — find cycle START. After meeting, reset slow to head; both step 1; they meet at cycle start. Math: distance head→start = distance meeting→start (mod cycle len).
floyd-cycle.287: Find Duplicate Number. Treat nums as a linked list — nums[i] is the 'next' pointer. Cycle MUST exist because some value repeats. Cycle start = the duplicate.
floyd-cycle.202: Happy Number. Treat digit-square-sum sequence as implicit list. Floyd detects cycle; if cycle reaches 1, happy; else unhappy.

bracket-match.20: Valid Parentheses. Push openers; on closer, top must match else fail. Empty stack at end ⇒ valid.
bracket-match.32: Longest Valid Parentheses. Stack of INDICES with −1 sentinel for 'last invalid before'. On '(' push i; on ')' pop; if stack empty push i as new sentinel; else max(answer, i − top).
bracket-match.921: Min Add to Make Parens Valid. Two counters: openNeeded, closeUnmatched. Single pass. Answer = sum at end.
bracket-match.1249: Min Remove to Make Valid. Pass 1: stack of '(' indices; pop on each ')'; leftover stack = '(' to remove; also collect unmatched ')'. Pass 2: build result skipping marked indices.

monotonic-deque.239: Sliding Window Maximum. Deque of INDICES, monotonic decreasing on values. For each i: pop front if i − k ≥ front; pop back while nums[back] < nums[i]; push i. Front is window max.
monotonic-deque.1438: Longest Subarray Abs Diff ≤ Limit. TWO deques — one max-decreasing, one min-increasing. For each r expand; while (max − min) > limit, shrink l updating both deques.
monotonic-deque.862: Shortest Subarray Sum ≥ K. Prefix sums; monotonic INCREASING deque of indices. For each i: while pre[i] − pre[front] ≥ K, pop front and update answer; while pre[back] ≥ pre[i], pop back (later prefix is better); push i.
monotonic-deque.918: Max Sum Circular Subarray. Alternative deque approach using prefix sums; standard solve is kadane-twice (see kadane note). Listed here for the deque option.
monotonic-deque.1696: Jump Game VI. dp[i] = nums[i] + max(dp[i−k..i−1]). Monotonic decreasing deque of dp values to get O(1) max-lookup over the sliding K window.

index-as-hash.41: First Missing Positive. Place each nums[i] at index nums[i]−1 via swapping (while in [1..n] and not already correct). Then find first i where nums[i] != i+1 ⇒ answer = i+1.
index-as-hash.268: Missing Number. Many ways: index-as-hash via swap-to-correct-slot; XOR (xor all + 0..n); or sum-formula (n(n+1)/2 − sum). All O(n) / O(1).
index-as-hash.287: Find Duplicate Number. Sign-flip variant: for each x, flip sign of nums[abs(x)−1]; if already negative, x is the duplicate. (Floyd's cycle is the other O(1)-space approach.)
index-as-hash.442: Find All Duplicates. Sign-flip: for each x, flip nums[abs(x)−1]; if already negative, append abs(x) to answer.
index-as-hash.448: Find All Disappeared Numbers. Sign-flip pass; indices STILL POSITIVE at end correspond to missing numbers (i+1).

bs-textbook.34: Find First and Last Position. Two binary searches — lower_bound (first ≥ target) and upper_bound (first > target). If lower_bound's value != target return [-1,-1].
bs-textbook.35: Search Insert Position. Plain lower_bound — return l at end (works whether target found or insertion point).
bs-textbook.704: Binary Search. Textbook l ≤ r loop; mid = l + (r-l)/2 to avoid overflow.
bs-textbook.278: First Bad Version. lower_bound on the bad-flag predicate; bad() is the monotone API.
bs-textbook.744: Smallest Letter Greater Than Target. upper_bound on chars; if past end, wrap to letters[0].
bs-textbook.540: Single Element in Sorted Array. Pairs at even indices; check if pair starting at mid (rounded down to even) is intact — if a[mid]==a[mid+1], single is to the right; else left.
bs-textbook.374: Guess Number Higher or Lower. Textbook BS using guess() API as the comparator.
bs-textbook.275: H-Index II (sorted). Find smallest i where citations[i] ≥ n − i. Answer = n − i.
bs-textbook.222: Count Complete Tree Nodes. Per subtree: compare full-left vs full-right depths; if equal, perfect subtree = 2^h − 1; else recurse both. Binary-search on last-level index gives O(log² n).
bs-textbook.436: Find Right Interval. Sort intervals by START with original index; for each interval's END, lower_bound to find first start ≥ end.
bs-textbook.74: Search a 2D Matrix. Treat as 1D flattened sorted array; mid → (mid/n, mid%n). O(log(m·n)).
bs-textbook.240: Search a 2D Matrix II. Rows+cols sorted but NOT globally — staircase from top-right (or bottom-left): on > target go left/down; on < go right/up. O(m+n).
bs-textbook.1351: Count Negatives Sorted Matrix. Each row sorted descending; per row, binary-search for first negative; accumulate (n − idx). Alternative: staircase like 240, O(m+n).

bs-on-answer.875: Koko Eating Bananas. Find min speed K such that totalHours(K) ≤ H. lo=1, hi=max(piles); feasibility is monotone in K.
bs-on-answer.1011: Capacity to Ship Packages in D Days. Find min capacity C s.t. shipsNeeded(C) ≤ D. lo=max(weights), hi=sum(weights).
bs-on-answer.410: Split Array Largest Sum. Find min largest-sum across K splits. lo=max(arr), hi=sum.
bs-on-answer.1482: Min Days to Make M Bouquets. Find min day d s.t. canMakeBouquets(d) ≥ m. Feasibility: scan and count contiguous runs ≥ k.
bs-on-answer.2141: Max Running Time of N Computers. Find max time t s.t. all n computers can run for t (sum of min(battery, t) across all ≥ n·t).
bs-on-answer.1898: Max Removable Chars Still Subseq. Find max k s.t. removing first k indices still leaves p as a subseq of s. Two-pointer check is the feasibility predicate.
bs-on-answer.2616: Min Max Diff via K Pairs. Find min threshold t s.t. we can form k disjoint pairs with |diff| ≤ t. Sort, greedy-pair adjacent.
bs-on-answer.2517: Max Tastiness of K-Candy Basket. Find max gap g s.t. we can pick k items with pairwise diff ≥ g. Sort + greedy feasibility.
bs-on-answer.719: K-th Smallest Pair Distance. Binary-search on distance value; countPairs(d) ≤ d uses sliding window after sort.
bs-on-answer.1648: Sell Diminishing-Valued Balls. Find max base sell-count k s.t. total balls sold (using floor-and-leftover) ≥ orders.

dfs-tree-orders.144: BT Preorder. visit, recurse left, recurse right. Iterative: stack of nodes; pop, visit, push right then left so left pops first.
dfs-tree-orders.94: BT Inorder. recurse left, visit, recurse right. Iterative: go-left pushing each, pop visit, then recurse right.
dfs-tree-orders.145: BT Postorder. recurse left, recurse right, visit. Iterative: easiest is modified preorder (root → right → left) collected in reverse.
dfs-tree-orders.543: Diameter. Post-order — return height (1 + max children); update global with leftHeight + rightHeight at current node.
dfs-tree-orders.124: BT Max Path Sum. Post-order — return max single-side gain CLAMPED to 0 (don't take negative subtrees); update global with leftGain + rightGain + node.val.

post-order-depth.104: Max Depth. 1 + max(leftDepth, rightDepth). Base null = 0.
post-order-depth.543: Diameter. At each node, candidate = leftDepth + rightDepth; return 1 + max(left, right) upward.
post-order-depth.110: Balanced Tree. Return height OR sentinel −1 if any subtree unbalanced. Propagate −1 upward to short-circuit.
post-order-depth.687: Longest Univalue Path. Per node return univalue-path-length downward; if child.val == node.val, length includes child; combine left + right at the node for the global max.
post-order-depth.1245: Tree Diameter (general N-ary graph). Same shape but n-ary; track TOP-2 child depths for diameter; or 2-BFS sweep.
post-order-depth.124: BT Max Path Sum. Return max single-side gain (clamped to 0); update global with left + right + val.
post-order-depth.222: Count Complete Tree Nodes. Hybrid post-order + binary-search: compare leftmost vs rightmost path lengths; if equal, perfect = 2^h − 1; else recurse both. O(log² n).

topo-sort.207: Course Schedule — can you finish? Kahn: queue of in-deg 0; decrement neighbours' in-deg; if final processed count == n, yes. Alternative: DFS 3-color cycle detect.
topo-sort.210: Course Schedule II — output order. Same Kahn; record pop order. Result is the topological ordering (any valid one).
topo-sort.269: Alien Dictionary. Build chars + edges from adjacent word pairs (first mismatch ⇒ a < b). Edge case: word1 is prefix of word2 with len1 > len2 ⇒ invalid. Then topo-sort.
topo-sort.444: Sequence Reconstruction. Kahn + UNIQUENESS check: at each step, EXACTLY ONE in-deg-0 node remains AND it matches the expected next of the original sequence.
topo-sort.802: Find Eventual Safe States. Reverse the graph; topo from out-deg-0 originals (sinks). Safe = nodes reaching a sink only.
topo-sort.2050: Parallel Courses III. Topo + DP — for each course, finishTime = max(prereqFinishes) + duration. Tracking max over a DAG.
topo-sort.1857: Largest Color Value in DAG. Topo + DP — count[v][color] = max over incoming neighbours; add 1 for v's own color.
topo-sort.1136: Parallel Courses. Topo by LEVELS (Kahn drains entire in-deg-0 batch per round); answer = number of rounds; −1 if cycle.
